measurements.source: gates.json, measure.json, plus a PIL ink-bbox pass on the 2550x3300 previews (300 dpi, 11.81 px/mm)

outer_margins_px.verdict: On both pages the left and right text margins agree within 0.6 mm and the bottom sits about 1 mm short of the sides, so they are borderline. gates.json safe_area_min_in is left 0.51 / right 0.594, a 2.1 mm mismatch that exceeds the ±1 mm tolerance for whatever element sets it. The front's top text margin is about 3 mm deeper than the bottom.

measurements.price_pair_scan: All 50 prices are inline and gap_em is 0.40 on letter (0.34 on phone), max 0.42, so every row passes and no price is remote. Format is whole dollars except Ranch Water 11.50, the only decimal price.
measurements.front_index_row_grid: The row tops align across all 4 columns (y about 1575/1990/2400 px at full size). The sensory lines do NOT share a baseline within a row, because wrapped two-line names push them down. Row 1: Margarita/Manhattan sensory line sits at about 1694 px, Brown Butter OF at about 1717 px, a 23 px (2.0 mm) step. Row 3 has the same 23 px step between 06/09/12 and 03. Column bottoms in the last index row are about 2685 / 2615 / 2685 / 2759 px, 144 px (12 mm) apart.
measurements.back_header_offset: The section labels (TEQUILA · BLANCO and so on) sit about 18 px (1.5 mm) above the first card-name line. Each group has a section rule plus a per-card top rule about 26 px (2.2 mm) below it, a double rule on every row.
measurements.back_dead_space: Column 4's last ink is at y=2808 against 3146 for columns 1-3, a 338 px (28.6 mm) shortfall. There are empty 4th-column card slots in Blanco row 2, Añejo and Casa (three holes of about 380x280 display px each), plus a void of about 230 px in the label column between VINO · WINE and the proposed key.
measurements.back_header_misplacement: VINO · WINE is set in the label column under CERVEZA Y SIDRA, but its items (Malbec, Pinot Grigio, Brut Rosé) sit in subgrid columns 3-4, so the header sits in a different column from its content.
measurements.contrast_worst_pixel: 6.72:1 minimum (muted note text on #F3F0E8), with no text below 4.5:1 on letter or phone
measurements.bleed: The front field and the back band run 9 px (3.175 mm) past trim, which passes. text_inside_safe=true.
measurements.visual_tests: front squint regions 4 with a single dominant primary (21:1), back squint regions 10 (fragmented); front/back silhouette_corr 0.485

top_problem: The back page's grid is not closed. The wine header sits in a different column from its wine. Column 4 stops 28.6 mm short, and three empty card slots plus a dead label column read as leftover canvas. The front breaks cross-column baselines by 2 mm whenever a name wraps. The boldest missing idea is an image system rooted in the place: the flavor map is a smart, ownable information idea, but its only art is a generic yellow-to-charcoal gradient that could sit on any bar's menu and fails the substitution test beside Rob's reference boards.
remove: The per-card top rules on the back (they double every section rule about 2 mm below it). Second candidate: the '—' placeholders for unknown region, which add 12 marks of noise with no data.
fixes: Move VINO · WINE out of the label column and set it as a subhead directly over Malbec / Pinot Grigio / Brut Rosé in columns 3-4, the same style and x as DE BARRIL · DRAFT.
Close the back grid: reflow the cards so every group fills whole 4-up rows, or collapse short groups (Añejo, Casa) into one shared row, so no column ends 28.6 mm early and no empty card slots remain.

On the front index, give each row a fixed two-line name slot (or hang the sensory line from the row's lowest name baseline) so the sensory, ingredient and garnish lines share one baseline across all four columns in each row.
Snap the back section labels to the first card-name baseline (drop them about 18 px / 1.5 mm) and delete the per-card top rule, so each group has one rule and one aligned entry line.

Give the field an image system with place in it: a printed-ink or risograph grain on the gradient, or plot marks drawn in one hand-lettered or engraved grammar tied to agave and Iowa corn, so the map passes the substitution test and stands beside the reference boards.

lens: typography and hierarchy: wordmark, section heads, item stack, numerals

measurements.source: No layout.elements were provided, so these are measured from preview-front.png and preview-back.png at 2550x3300 (display coordinates x1.65), plus gates.json and measure.json
measurements.front_item_name_left_edges_px: 309 / 878 / 1447 / 2015 in cols 1-4, each constant within its column (pass)
measurements.front_row_pitch_px: row1 to row2 = 408, row2 to row3 = 406, within 0.5 mm (pass)
measurements.front_sensory_line_baseline_drift_in_one: about 21 px (1.8 mm) in row 1 (col1/col2 vs col3) and row 3 (col1/col3 vs col2/col4). Names that wrap (Brown Butter Old / Fashioned, Ranch / Water, Mezcal / Negroni, Milpa Old / Fashioned, Spicy Pineapple / Margarita) push the stack down, so there is no shared baseline grid across a row (fail on criterion 1's 100-bar, not capped)
measurements.price_format: MIXED: 11.50 (Ranch Water) beside whole-number prices on the same page. This is a scorecard criterion 3 auto-fail, so it is capped at 40
measurements.wordmark: 'Cantina' in Inter Tight bold at about 48 pt, with '& Cocktail Bar · Iowa City, Iowa' at 9.75 pt: a 4.9:1 size ratio, so the ampersand line reads as an afterthought and not as part of the name
measurements.numeral_systems: Two styles key the same data: disc badges are heavy bold numerals reversed out of black circles, and the index keys are Inter Tight 200 hairline at about 60 pt. The index numerals out-shout the item names (cap height about 2.3x the names)
measurements.back_head_levels: Level-2 sub-heads (DE BARRIL, EN LATA, SIDRA, POR COPA, ESPUMOSOS) use exactly the same tracked caps, size and weight as the level-1 section labels (TEQUILA · BLANCO, CERVEZA Y SIDRA, VINO · WINE), so two levels share one style. 'VINO · WINE' sits in the label column about 1,300 px left of its items in cols 3-4, stacked under the beer head. 'POR COPA · BY THE GLASS' and 'ESPUMOSOS · SPARKLING' break onto two lines
measurements.back_redundancy: The italic class line repeats its group head on 25 cards ('reposado' x8 under TEQUILA · REPOSADO). Region placeholder '—' prints 9 times
measurements.dead_space: Back: empty 4th card slot in the Blanco row 2, Añejo and Casa rows. Front: about 150 px of unused field below zero-proof, plus a two-line reserved name slot above the class line on single-line spirit cards
measurements.contrast_worst_pixel_min: 6.72:1 (muted grotesk on paper). Badges are at least 16:1 and band text at least 10.4:1 (from gates.json; pass)
measurements.bleed: 3.175 mm on the front field and back band (pass)

remove: The italic class line on each of the 25 spirit cards ('blanco', 'reposado', ...): it repeats the group head, and the oak bar already encodes class. Cutting it also closes the reserved gap under single-line names.
top_problem: The type system is a strong Swiss data idea let down at the item level: the hairline index numerals are the loudest thing in the stack, names wrap in a narrow measure and break the row baselines, and the back flattens two head levels into one style. It reads as a well-built infographic, not a finished menu. The single boldest missing idea is typographic ownership: the wordmark is plain Inter Tight 'Cantina', with nothing drawn from the field or the axis language that would make the name as memorable as the map.
fixes: Print Ranch Water as '11½' or set every price to one format, so the menu has a single price format and criterion 3 is released from the 40 cap.

Set each index row on a fixed baseline grid: reserve two name lines on every cocktail (or widen the name measure by tucking the numeral into a narrower hanging column), so sensory, ingredient and garnish lines share baselines across all four columns.

Drop the index numerals to about 60% of their current size, or into a muted ink tint, so the name (bold, larger) is the dominant step in the stack. Also match the numeral style of the disc badges and the index keys (both hairline, or both bold), so one numeral system keys the map.

Create a distinct level-2 head style on the back (for example sentence-case small bold or italic serif) for DE BARRIL / EN LATA / SIDRA / POR COPA / ESPUMOSOS. Move 'VINO · WINE' so it heads cols 3-4 directly over its items, and shorten the labels so none break onto two lines.

Give the wordmark a drawn gesture from the concept (for example 'Cantina' set with an axis rule or plotted baseline), and set '& Cocktail Bar' in the same weight family at a closer size ratio, so the venue name is ownable and not default Inter bold.

lens: palette, contrast over the art, price and number styling

measurements.palette_hex_in_menu_html: ink #161513 (416 uses), paper #F3F0E8 (229), ink tints #34322E and #57534B, rule #E4DCCB; colour only in the field: yellow #F4DA3C / #EDBE38, ochre #B98039, browns #5A4536 / #4A2E23, Campari red #B2352C
measurements.field_samples_front_px: left edge (244,218,60), mid (196,142,56), right edge (61,50,42): the middle third reads as muddy ochre-brown, not a deliberate second colour
measurements.contrast_worst_pixel: gates.json minimum is 6.72:1 (#57534B muted grotesk on paper, front, back and phone). Ink #161513 on the brightest field yellow (244,218,60) measures 12.98:1. White numerals on the black badges measure at least 16:1. All reading text sits on flat paper, so no text sits on the art at all.
measurements.price_format: FAIL (mixed formats): 49 prices are whole numbers ('15', '12') and one is 'Ranch Water 11.50'. The scorecard's 'same format everywhere, decimals or none' rule caps criterion 3 at 40.
measurements.price_position: All prices are inline, with a max gap of 0.42 em from the name (gates.json). There is no price column, so eye travel is 0% and the remote-price check does not apply.
measurements.price_styling: Prices are set in Inter Tight regular at name size, next to semibold names. The hairline 'proposed' ring sits right after the numeral ('Paloma 12 ○', 'Clase Azul Reposado 26 ○'), and in dim light it reads as a trailing zero or a degree sign. It appears on 30+ rows, so it is the most frequent mark on either page.
measurements.number_styling: The Inter Tight 200 index numerals 01-12 and the 0/12/24/36/48 scale are the best number work in the set. But the index numerals (about 60 px tall) are 4x the prices, so the index number wins over the name and the price.
measurements.back_colour: 0% accent on the back (visual_tests.json). The front colour system does not carry over.
measurements.dead_space: Front: the x axis is set below the field on bare paper, leaving a roughly 55 px detached strip, and the paper under zero-proof is empty down to about 1.9k/2k. Back: empty card slots at Blanco row 2 col 4, Añejo col 4 and Casa col 4, plus an unused label-column block beside the beer and wine block.
measurements.bleed: The front field bleeds 3.175 mm top and right, and the back band bleeds top, left and right (gates.json). Pass.

remove: The '+' registration-dot grid inside the flavour field. It adds texture to the gradient but no information, and it muddies the ochre middle. The discs and the axes already carry the plot.
top_problem: The palette is one gradient that goes muddy in the middle, and it vanishes on the back. The design is missing a real colour idea rooted in the venue, for example a two-ink system (a citrus or chile accent plus ink) that carries across both pages and marks prices and section keys with intent.
fixes: Unify the price format: print 11.50 as a whole-number style that fits the set (for example 11½ in a tabular figure), or print every price with two decimals. One format everywhere lifts criterion 3 off the 40 cap.
Move the 'proposed' ring off the price baseline: put it before the name or superscript it, and make it visibly not a numeral, so '12 ○' can never read as '120' or '12°' in bar light.

Replace the linear yellow-to-charcoal gradient with two or three stepped, named flat inks (a lime/citrus yellow, a roasted-agave amber, a smoke charcoal) so the middle stops going muddy brown. Then use the amber once on the back, in the oak bars or the band numerals, so both pages share one palette.

Give prices a deliberate figure style: tabular lining figures in a medium weight, one step darker than the ingredients. Bring the 60 px index numerals down, or make them a tint, so name and price lead the item stack rather than the key number.
Pull the x-axis ('Bright → Rich') onto the field edge or into the field, and fill or collapse the empty back card slots, so no stretch of bare paper is left without a job.

margins_px_at_300dpi.top_front_first_text: ~198 (wordmark cap; about 4 mm more than the bottom, so the page sits slightly low)

measurements.bleed: front field bleeds 3.175 mm top and right, back band bleeds top/left/right: pass. But the x axis sits on paper about 60 px below the field's bottom edge, so the plot and its own axis are detached.
measurements.price_pair: inline, max gap 0.42 em, no remote prices: pass
measurements.price_format: FAIL: '11.50' (Ranch Water) is the only decimal price among 49 whole-dollar prices, which is a mixed format (scorecard criterion 3 automatic fail, so it is capped at 40)
measurements.contrast_worst_pixel: min 6.72:1 (muted grotesk on paper). Badges on the field are at least 16:1: pass
measurements.front_index_name_wraps: 4 of 12 names wrap unnecessarily (Ranch/Water, Mezcal/Negroni, Milpa Old/Fashioned, Brown Butter Old/Fashioned) because each 2-digit Inter Tight 200 numeral takes about 30% of a roughly 300 px (display) column
measurements.back_empty_cells: 4 unused card slots (Blanco row 2 col 4, Añejo col 4, Casa col 4, and the left rail between the Beer/Wine labels and the legend), plus about 120 px of dead space under the wine columns
measurements.back_null_data: 10 of 25 region fields print '—' and 4 of 25 oak tracks are empty, so about 30% of the back's data marks encode 'unknown'
measurements.back_redundancy: class is encoded three times per card: the group label, the italic class word, and an oak bar that is identical within each group
measurements.visual_tests: front primary:secondary 21.5, accent 14.7% all inside the field. Back primary is the ink band (200:1)

remove: The italic class word on every spirit card (blanco / reposado / añejo / mezcal espadín, 25 times). The group label and the oak bar already state it, so it is the third encoding of the same fact and adds a line of height to every card.
top_problem: The flavor field is a smart, honest information idea, but it has been seen before (flavor-quadrant menus are now common in serious cocktail bars) and it is not rooted in this venue. Swap the wordmark and it is any bar's taste chart: the Swiss grotesk, the CSS-looking linear gradient and the app-like icon discs carry no Mexico and no Iowa, and have no material presence. The concept governs the top half of the front only. The index below is ordered by category, not by the map, so the reader has to jump map -> number -> list. On the back the oak bars repeat per-class facts rather than per-bottle ones, so the data system looks rigorous but is mostly redundant or empty. The boldest missing idea: make the field the menu itself. Set each drink's name and price on the field at its coordinate, or order and number the index along a single bright-to-smoky path so the list reads as a walk across the map. Then give the field a material and cultural source (for example, the gradient as an actual lime-to-roasted-agave-to-mezcal-ash ink sequence printed as a flat spot-colour split fountain with visible grain, not a screen gradient). Next to Solstice and Glass Garden it is cleaner and more truthful, but it has no image system, no materiality and no emotional pull: it reads as an infographic, not a cantina.
fixes: Resolve the mixed price format: have the owner confirm a whole-dollar price for Ranch Water, or print one consistent format across the menu. As is, the single '11.50' fails criterion 3.

Make the concept govern the index: renumber the 12 drinks along one bright/clean -> rich/smoky path (03, 02, 08, 01, 10, 05 ... 09) and order the index in that sequence, with Clásicos and De la Casa marked by a small tag rather than by column, so map and list read as one route. Alternatively, set the name and price beside each disc on the field and cut the lookup step.

Replace the screen-flat linear gradient (whose muddy olive-brown midzone reads as UI) with a printable, concept-justified material: two or three flat spot inks (lime yellow, roasted agave amber, mezcal-ash charcoal) stepped in bands or a split fountain with real grain. Bring the x axis inside the field's bottom edge so the plate and its axis are one object.
Fix the front index cell: shrink the display numerals to about 60% or place them above the name, so no cocktail name wraps and the name/sensory/ingredient stack gets the full column measure.

On the back, drop the per-card class word, fill or collapse the four empty card slots (re-flow Añejo + Casa into one row set), and give Beer and Wine their own left-rail labels aligned to their content rather than stacked together above the legend.

lens: phone version (preview-phone.png, 1170x18831, cropped) and print/phone coherence

measurements.phone_map_render: BROKEN. In the phone map band (y 370-1660 px), the glass glyphs render as huge ink silhouettes, apparently an unscaled rocks-glass shape, and cover about 80% of the field. Paper discs and ink badges are gone, and only the white numerals float on flat black. The gradient is visible only in the top-left ~15%. A stray glyph fragment sits beside 12. The designer's own phone-part1.png shows the same thing, so it shipped unnoticed; gates.json does not check it.
measurements.phone_axes: On the phone, the axes are removed from the map and replaced by a caption line ('Bright → Rich, left to right / Clean → Smoky, bottom to top'), so the plot has no axis.
measurements.contrast_worst_pixel: 6.72:1 muted grotesk on paper (front/back/phone); map numerals are white on #141311, above 15:1
measurements.price_pair_gap_em: max 0.42 em inline on letter and phone; no remote prices; eye-travel fraction 0%
measurements.left_edges: print index names share one x per column; phone index single left edge at 138/746 display px after numerals: pass
measurements.print_name_wraps: Short names break beside the 64 pt numerals: 'Ranch / Water', 'Mezcal / Negroni', 'Milpa Old / Fashioned'
measurements.phone_spirit_cards: The 2-up cards keep the print micro-card grid at 390 css px. When a name wraps in one card, the class/track rows fall at different heights across the pair, leaving empty bands of about 1 line per card, and many cards print '—' as their region.
measurements.header_levels: Print back sets 'Cerveza y sidra · Beer & cider' as a tracked-caps label. The phone sets it as a sentence-case display head the size of 'Destilados · Spirits', so the same level has two styles across the two media.
measurements.dead_space: Letter front and back end within ~5% of the bottom margin (pass). Phone: dead gaps in the spirit cards, and the map band is ~1290 px of mostly flat black.
measurements.bleed: front field 3.175 mm top/right, back band top/left/right: pass

remove: The '+' crosshair lattice inside the field. On the phone it shows as five orphan crosses above the black mass, and in print it competes with the discs without carrying data.
top_problem: The phone's first screen, the hero of the whole concept, is a broken render: runaway glyph silhouettes black out the flavor field, the discs are gone and the axes are stripped, so the phone reads as a different, unfinished menu. Beyond the bug, the biggest missing idea is a cultural one. The Swiss data-plot could belong to any cocktail bar anywhere: nothing in the field's material, palette or mark-making is rooted in Mexico or Iowa (for example, amate/loess paper tones, or a corn-to-agave ground). It is well short of the reference boards, and the print front alone would sit around the high 70s.
fixes: Fix the phone map SVG. Give every glass glyph symbol an explicit viewBox and a fixed width/height of about 36-40 css px, restore the paper discs and ink number badges, and add a visual test that fails when the phone map's dark-pixel share differs from the letter map's by more than 10%.
Draw the Bright→Rich and Clean→Smoky axes with arrows and end labels on the phone map itself, as the letter front does, rather than as a caption line, so one plot grammar holds across both media.

Rebuild the phone spirit section as one-column rows (name + price / class / oak bar / region) with the oak track at one fixed x and y inside each row, and omit the '—' region placeholders, to remove the empty bands the 2-up cards create at 390 px.

On letter, stop short names wrapping beside the index numerals (Ranch Water, Mezcal Negroni, Milpa Old Fashioned) by cutting the numerals from about 64 pt to about 48 pt or letting the name run full column width, and bring the right safe inset to within 1 mm of the left (currently 2.1 mm wider).

Unify price format and header levels across media: set 11.50 in a consistent style (for example, tabular figures with matching decimals where any decimal appears in the section, subject to Rob's price source), and use the same tracked-caps style for Beer & cider / Wine on phone and print.

lens: every item and price, checked against expanded-v1/manifest.json
top_problem: The flavor map prints a flavor claim for each drink that the manifest does not make. The front caption says 'Each cocktail sits where its sensory notes and ingredients place it', but the y axis is labelled Smoky. It puts Carajillo at 5.9 (above the midline, level with the mezcal drinks), Milpa at 5.3, Brown Butter Old Fashioned at 4.3 and Manhattan at 3.3. None of those manifest sensory lines or ingredient lists says smoke. The placements come from the designer's untasted inference ('espresso roast', 'barrel char'), so guests read an invented item fact.
problems: Price check: I diffed menu.html independently against the manifest. All 50 items are present: 12 cocktails, 25 spirits, 6 beer/cider, 3 wine and 4 zero-proof. Every price matches, no item is extra, and every sensory line, ingredient, garnish, glass, class and region prints exactly and in manifest order. The ring key matches the status on every row I checked: Margarita, Manhattan, Brown Butter Old Fashioned, House Daiquiri and the house pours have no ring, and every PROPOSED or rob_reference_image row has one.

content_integrity fails on the map's y axis. 'Smoky' is an item-level claim for Carajillo, Milpa, Brown Butter Old Fashioned and Manhattan that no manifest text supports. The small disclaimer 'Placement is a PHG inference... not a tasting panel' contradicts the larger caption, which says the placement comes from the menu text.

Price format is mixed: Ranch Water prints '11.50' while the other 49 prices are whole numbers. The value is faithful to the manifest's 11.5, but the one decimal breaks format consistency (criterion 3). The name also breaks as 'Ranch / Water 11.50', which makes it the weakest name-price unit on the front.

Missing facts are not flagged. Beer has style but no ABV, wine has grape but no region, Brut Rosé has no grape, and zero-proof has no ingredients. None of these is marked missing_ingredients on the menu or in proposal.md (only zero-proof is mentioned there). The manifest note 'glass or bottle unknown (needs_input 5)' for Brut Rosé is dropped, so it prints with no serve label under Espumosos.

Internal placeholders reach the guest page. Twelve spirit cards print '—' where the manifest region is null. The mezcal prices are marked 'PRICE PLACEHOLDER' in the manifest but print as ordinary prices with only the generic proposed ring, so the guest page does not show the placeholder status.

Categories are not treated equally, and the back's reading path breaks at the bottom. Spirits get the full-bleed hero band and 25 cards. Beer, cider and wine are squeezed into one bottom band where both category heads ('CERVEZA Y SIDRA · BEER & CIDER' / 'VINO · WINE') are stacked in the label column. The wine head sits two columns away from the wine items, and draft beer snakes across two columns with Cans and Cider tucked underneath.
In the Casa · House pours group, the label line only describes Cognac VSOP. The house Blanco Tequila and Añejo Tequila cards get no class line in their own group, unlike every other group.
fixes: Rework the y axis so every drink with no smoke or roast word in its manifest text sits in the bottom band (y ≤ 2), or rename the axis to what the text supports (for example 'Clean → Smoky / Roasted'). Also change the caption so it matches the 'PHG inference' disclaimer instead of claiming the placement comes from the menu text.
Ask Rob to settle Ranch Water at a whole-dollar price (not the designer's call), and until then keep 'Ranch Water' unbroken on one line with its price.

Label the Brut Rosé serve ('glass' / 'bottle') once Rob answers needs_input 5. Meanwhile list the missing data in proposal.md as missing_ingredients: beer ABV, wine region, Brut Rosé grape and zero-proof ingredients.

Give beer/cider and wine each their own head in the column above their own items. Run draft beer down one column so it cannot be read in two orders. Give the back's bottom band enough height that these categories are not visibly an afterthought to spirits.

Remove the guest-facing '—' region placeholders: leave the slot empty or hold those cards until the regions are verified. Give the placeholder mezcal prices a distinct 'price TBC' marker rather than only the generic proposed ring.
note: Phone preview not inspected (tool budget); criterion 10 is scored on print only.

lens: ingredient names, sensory lines, description completeness
top_problem: The cocktail stack is complete. Everywhere else the menu shows gaps in the descriptions without flagging them. Spicy Pineapple Margarita prints only 'jalapeño-infused tequila blanco · fresh pineapple': a margarita with no citrus or liqueur, although the manifest source says 'confirm liqueur/citrus'. The 4 zero-proof drinks have no ingredients and no garnish/glass line, so items 3 and 4 of Rob's binding stack are missing. None of the 6 beers shows an ABV. None of the 3 wines shows a region. Brut Rosé ('glass or bottle unknown', needs_input 5) is printed with no pour label and no flag. None of these gaps is flagged missing_ingredients on the menu or in proposal.md's open items.
problems: Content source check: I compared all 50 names and prices against expanded-v1/manifest.json by eye on both previews. All of them match, including 11.5, printed as 11.50. There are no invented, changed or dropped items. The DE BARRIL, EN LATA, POR COPA and ESPUMOSOS subheads come from the manifest's own group keys, so they are not invented.
The ring after the price is correct on every PROPOSED and rob_reference_image row. Approved rows carry no ring.
No taglines, side-rail slogans or prop captions state an item fact. The front caption and the note 'Placement is a PHG inference … not a tasting panel' are generic and honest.
Spicy Pineapple Margarita has no citrus or liqueur and no garnish; its garnish · glass line reads only 'rocks'. It needs a missing_ingredients flag, not silence.

Zero-proof shows only a sensory line: no ingredients and no garnish · glass. Nojito's 'Mint, lime, soda' does double duty as both sensory line and ingredient list. Horchata 'Rice, cinnamon, creamy' blurs the same way.
Beer rows have a style (in the sensory line) but no ABV (criterion 8). Wine rows have the grape but no region. 'Dry red wine' and 'Dry white wine' are taxonomy wording, not guest language.
Brut Rosé sits under 'Espumosos · Sparkling' with no glass or bottle label. The manifest marks this as unknown (needs_input 5), and the menu does not show it as pending.

In the Casa · House Pours group, only Cognac VSOP gets a sensory line. Blanco Tequila and Añejo Tequila have their sensory text only in the Blanco and Añejo group labels higher up the page, so a guest reading the house row does not see it.
Each spirit card repeats its class in italic ('blanco' under TEQUILA · BLANCO), which uses space without adding information. That slot could carry the item's own sensory line.

Carajillo's plot position (y 5.9, smokier than Milpa and Manhattan) comes from espresso roast, not smoke. Placing it on a 'Smoky' axis reads as a flavour claim the manifest's sensory line ('Espresso, vanilla, bittersweet') does not make. Manhattan's 'barrel char' reasoning is also not in the manifest text.

Names wrap needlessly because the 200-weight index numerals take so much width: 'Ranch / Water 11.50', 'Mezcal / Negroni', 'Milpa Old / Fashioned'. The prices are still bound to the name, but a two-word name should not break.
Price format: every price is a whole number except 11.50, so one row carries decimals. The ring directly after a number ('12 ○') can read as a degree sign at a glance.

Section flow on the back: spirits come before beer and wine, which suits an agave-led cantina. But the beer and wine sit cramped in the bottom band. 'Vino · Wine' is stacked under the beer head in the label column, two columns away from the wine rows it names.
fixes: Flag the unknowns in print and in proposal.md: mark missing_ingredients on the Spicy Pineapple Margarita (citrus/liqueur and garnish) and on all 4 zero-proof drinks, and add these to Rob's open-items list rather than printing them as if complete.
Mark beer ABV and wine region as 'pending' (or list them as needs_input) so beer reads style + ABV and wine reads grape + region once data arrives. Show Brut Rosé's glass or bottle status as pending.

Replace the redundant italic class line on each spirit card with that item's own sensory line, or at least print the sensory lines for the house Blanco Tequila and Añejo Tequila in the Casa group label.
Move 'Vino · Wine' so it sits directly above its two wine columns, as a subhead aligned with POR COPA and ESPUMOSOS, not stacked under the beer head in the left label column.
Re-plot Carajillo (and Manhattan) using only the manifest's words: roast is not smoke. Alternatively, rename the y axis 'Clean → Roasted/Smoky' so the placement does not imply a smoke claim.

lens: Flow and reading path for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City, front and back (K3 MAPA DE SABOR, /home/user/phg-harmony-app/handoff/designs/test-1-iowa-city-cantina/explore-K3/)
top_problem: Neither page has a clean reading path. On the front, the dominant field carries only numbers, so a guest who wants a Margarita has to jump to the index. The index then runs column-major (Clásicos 01-06 down columns 1-2, Casa 07-12 down columns 3-4), but the four columns share row baselines and huge 01/04/07/10 numerals, so the eye reads across the rows and mixes the classic and house drinks. On the back, beer and wine are squeezed into a footer strip. The one label column stacks 'CERVEZA Y SIDRA' and 'VINO · WINE' together at far left, while the wine itself sits two columns away under its own subheads. In an Iowa City cantina, Modelo and Tecate are volume sellers, and here they are the hardest thing on the menu to find.
problems: Content check against expanded-v1/manifest.json: all 50 items and prices match. Every name and price was checked by eye on both pages, and gates.json reports DOM diff 0. Proposed rings match status: Margarita, Manhattan, Brown Butter Old Fashioned, House Daiquiri, the three Casa pours, the in-house beers and the wines carry no ring; every PROPOSED and rob_reference_image row has one. Side-rail copy ('Each cocktail sits where...', 'Placement is a PHG inference...', 'Each card: name and price, class, months in oak, region') is explanation, not item fact. No taglines.
Mixed price format: Ranch Water prints '11.50' while every other price on both pages is a whole number. This is not a changed price, but it breaks one-format consistency (criterion 3).

The front index is column-major, but its grid reads as row-major. Rows 01/04/07/10, 02/05/08/11 and 03/06/09/12 share baselines, and the only thing splitting Clásicos from Casa is the header rule over columns 3-4. The 60 px light numerals outweigh the item names, so the numbers become the focal layer instead of the drinks.

The map has no names or prices. The top 40% of the front is the entry point but cannot be ordered from, so every choice needs a second look-up in the index. That is acceptable for discovery, but a first-time guest has to hunt.
Back: the 'VINO · WINE' section head sits in the label column under the beer head, not above its items (Malbec, Pinot Grigio, Brut Rosé in columns 3-4). The head is detached from its section.

Back: beer, cider and wine together get about 17% of the page, at the bottom, while 25 spirit pours get about 70%. The brief asks for every drinks category to be treated equally, and here beer and wine read like a footnote. For this venue, Mexican beer belongs in view, not in a trailing strip.

Back: the Casa house pours Blanco Tequila and Añejo Tequila print no sensory line of their own. Their class lines sit in the Tequila Blanco and Tequila Añejo group labels several rows above, so the description is detached from the item. Cognac VSOP's and Ilegal Joven's lines sit in the label column, named but away from their cards.

Spirit cards with one-line names leave an empty line before the class, while cards with two-line names do not. The internal rhythm of the cards is uneven across each row (for example Espolòn Blanco next to Olmeca Altos Plata).

Criterion 8: beers print no ABV, and wines print no grape/region detail beyond 'Dry red wine' and similar. Brut Rosé has 'glass or bottle unknown (needs_input 5)' in the manifest, but the menu shows no pour label and the proposal's open items do not flag it. Carajillo and Spicy Pineapple Margarita have null garnish and print glass only, with no missing-info flag. Nothing is invented, but the missing facts are not flagged.
Order: spirits are reordered so Casa pours come last, which differs from the manifest but follows the brief. For an agave-focused venue it is defensible.
fixes: Make the index row-major within each section, or give Clásicos and Casa visibly separate blocks (a gutter rule or a top offset), and cut the index numerals to about 1.3x the name size so names lead.

Give the back's beer/cider and wine each a head in the label column aligned with its own row, promote Mexican beer (Modelo, Tecate) out of the footer, and balance the space (for example compress the spirit cards' empty class line) so beer and wine get full rows.
Print each Casa pour's class sensory line on or directly beside its own card, rather than relying on the blanco and añejo group labels above.
Print Ranch Water as '11.5', or, if Rob prefers decimals, set every price with one decimal convention; do not mix formats.

Flag the missing data in the proposal's open items and ask for it: beer ABV and style detail, wine grape and region, Brut Rosé glass or bottle (needs_input 5), and garnish for Carajillo and Spicy Pineapple Margarita.

lens: Description quality and whether the menu speaks in one guest-facing voice (K3 MAPA DE SABOR, /home/user/phg-harmony-app/handoff/designs/test-1-iowa-city-cantina/explore-K3/). Every printed item fact checked against expanded-v1/manifest.json. No DB queries were run because the manifest is the designated content source.
top_problem: The menu speaks in two voices. The cocktail sensory lines are guest language ('Smoke, bitter orange, velvet', 'Green heat, ripe pineapple'), but the rest of the copy reads like chart instructions or internal notes. Front-page legend: 'Each cocktail sits where its sensory notes and ingredients place it. The numbers key to the index below', 'Cube: served on ice. Tint: shown only where an ingredient sets the colour' (British spelling on a US menu) and 'Placement is a PHG inference from the menu text, not a tasting panel' (the internal company name printed for guests). Back-page legend: 'Each card: name and price, class, months in oak, region. Empty track: age not stated.' On the back, the 25 spirit cards repeat the item name as taxonomy: 'Espolòn Blanco' then 'blanco', 'Hornitos Reposado' then 'reposado', 'Don Julio Blanco' then 'blanco'. Missing regions show as a bare '—' on 11 cards, which is a database null, not guest language. Beer and wine lines mostly restate the name or category: 'Dry-Hopped IPA / Hop-forward draft IPA', 'Dry Cider / Dry sparkling cider', 'Amber Lager / Toasty amber lager', 'Malbec / Dry red wine', 'Pinot Grigio / Dry white wine'. These are the scorecard's criterion-12 failure pattern. All facts trace to the manifest: cocktail rows match (Margarita from rv f06abb74, Manhattan 9fb77eaa, Brown Butter Old Fashioned 7095fd3d, House Daiquiri 14d45e57, Rob-reference and PROPOSED rows as listed), spirit class and region match each manifest row (for example Corralejo = Guanajuato, Herradura and Fortaleza = Tequila Valley), and every PROPOSED or rob_reference_image item carries the ring. So content_integrity passes. Caveat: every sensory line except the Margarita's is manifest status 'draft_not_tasted'. The approved items (Manhattan, Brown Butter Old Fashioned, House Daiquiri) print them unringed, as settled fact.
problems: Voice split. Guest sensory lines sit beside chart-legend and internal copy: 'Placement is a PHG inference…', 'Each card: name and price, class, months in oak, region', 'Empty track: age not stated', 'Tint: shown only where an ingredient sets the colour' ('colour' is British; the rest of the menu uses US spelling, e.g. 'flavors' on Jarritos).

Taxonomy wording on the spirit cards. The italic class line repeats the name and the section head (blanco / reposado / añejo) and says nothing sensory. The actual sensory lines were moved into the section heads, so no individual pour has a description.

Placeholder '—' printed for a null region on Espolòn, Milagro, Siete Leguas? no (Los Altos); on Espolòn, Milagro, Casamigos, Hornitos, Teremana, Casa Noble, Clase Azul and the three house pours. The manifest region is null for these, so the dash is honest, but it is database output shown to guests.

Exception copy wedged into section heads. The mezcal head carries 'Ilegal Joven: Unaged, pit-roasted · smoke, citrus peel' (capital U mid-line). The CASA head describes only 'Cognac VSOP: 4+ years oak · stone fruit, toffee'. The Blanco Tequila and Añejo Tequila house pours have manifest sensory lines that are not printed next to them.

Beer, cider and wine descriptions repeat the name or category (IPA, Amber Lager, Dry Cider, Malbec 'Dry red wine', Pinot Grigio 'Dry white wine'). Malbec and Pinot Grigio print no region or style detail. The source has none, so this is a flag-and-ask item, not something to invent.

Brut Rosé 13 sits under ESPUMOSOS with no glass or bottle label, next to the POR COPA column. The manifest flags glass/bottle as unknown (needs_input 5), but the page does not mark it, so a guest will assume a glass.
Cocktail sensory lines are nearly one voice (comma triplets). The Margarita breaks the pattern with 'Bright and citrus-forward', and 'Crisp, clean, lightly rich' (House Daiquiri) contradicts itself.

Name wraps split the item stack. 'Ranch / Water 11.50', 'Mezcal / Negroni 15', 'Brown Butter Old / Fashioned 16' and 'Milpa Old / Fashioned 15' break inside a fixed phrase and push the price onto a second line. On the back, 'Hornitos / Reposado 9' and similar cards do the same. The huge 01–12 numerals take the width the names need.

Spirits age scale header '0 12 24 36 48' has no unit on the axis itself; 'months' appears only in the legend sentence. Cognac VSOP plotted as an arrow on a tequila oak scale reads as a data chart, not a menu.

Venue fit is decent. The Spanish/English pairing is consistent and correct: Cócteles, Clásicos, De la casa, Destilados, De barril, En lata, Sidra, Por copa, Espumosos, Sin alcohol. Iowa hooks (Loess, Iowa wildflower honey, Milpa corn) suit Iowa City. But the stacked left-column labels 'CERVEZA Y SIDRA · BEER & CIDER / VINO · WINE' float away from their sub-columns, and 'Loess' gets no guest-facing cue.
fixes: Rewrite every legend and caption in guest voice, or cut it, and drop 'PHG inference' entirely. For example 'Brighter to the left, richer to the right; smokier toward the top' and 'Bars show time in oak.' Change 'colour' to 'color'.
On each spirit card, replace the italic class line (which repeats the name) with the manifest's sensory line for that class, or remove it. Show a missing region as blank space, not '—'.
Put the Blanco Tequila and Añejo Tequila house pours' manifest sensory lines on their own cards. Move the Ilegal Joven and Cognac exception lines out of the section heads and onto those cards.

Stop the beer, cider and wine lines from repeating their names. Use only manifest facts (style, 'on draft', 'in the can'), and flag Malbec, Pinot Grigio and Brut Rosé region / pour size as missing_ingredients or needs_input rather than filling the space with 'Dry red wine'. Label Brut Rosé's pour once needs_input 5 is answered.

Layout note for the designer: reduce the index numerals or widen the name measure so cocktail names and prices do not break mid-phrase ('Ranch Water', 'Mezcal Negroni', 'Old Fashioned'). Keep name + price on one line, as Rob's item stack requires.

lens: How descriptions and prices sit together in the print PNGs (front 2550x3300, back 2550x3300), plus the price-to-item gate. Checked against expanded-v1/manifest.json.
top_problem: The price-and-description unit is correct but the layout is cramped. On the front, the 200-weight index numerals take about a third of each column, which leaves roughly 22 characters for the rest. As a result, 4 of 12 names break over two lines with the price on the second line ('Ranch / Water 11.50', 'Mezcal / Negroni 15', 'Milpa Old / Fashioned 15', 'Brown Butter Old / Fashioned 16'). Ingredient lines also break inside a single ingredient ('orange / liqueur', 'sweet / vermouth', 'fresh / lime' in 08, 'Iowa / wildflower'), and the Loess sensory line leaves 'snap' alone on its own line. Separately, the back prints '1.5 oz pour' as a fact in the Spirits header. The manifest says pour_size = '1.5 oz proposed standard pour (not established)', and the header has no ring flag, so it is an unflagged proposal presented as fact. That fails content_integrity under this panel's rule that proposals must be flagged.
problems: content_integrity FAIL: back band 'Destilados · Spirits / 1.5 oz pour'. Source: manifest.json pour_size = '1.5 oz proposed standard pour (not established)'. It is printed without the proposed ring or any 'pending' wording, unlike every proposed item row.

Brut Rosé 13 (manifest note: 'glass or bottle unknown (needs_input 5)') sits under 'Espumosos · Sparkling' with no serve unit. The 'Por copa · By the glass' header covers only Malbec and Pinot Grigio, so a guest cannot tell whether 13 buys a glass or a bottle. Nothing false is printed, but the price reads without a unit.

Front index measure is too narrow: names wrap in 01-12 where they need not (03 'Ranch Water' is two short words split over two lines). Ingredient lines break mid-ingredient ('orange / liqueur' in 01, 'sweet / vermouth' in 04 and 09, 'house / demerara syrup' in 08, 'Iowa / wildflower honey syrup' in 12), which breaks role-order scanning. The 12 sensory line has a one-word widow, 'snap'.

Back cards: 9 of 25 regions print as a bare em dash (manifest region null, e.g. Espolòn Blanco, Milagro Silver, Casamigos Blanco, Hornitos, Teremana, Casa Noble, Clase Azul, all three Casa pours). At print size these read as missing data under the price, not as 'not stated'. The key says 'Empty track: age not stated' but explains nothing about the dash.

Ilegal Joven's own sensory line (manifest: 'Unaged, pit-roasted · smoke, citrus peel') is printed in the MEZCAL label column, about 860 px from its card, while its card shows only 'mezcal espadín joven'. Because the line names the item, association holds, but the description is physically split from its name and price.
The proposed ring sits a word-space after the price ('12 ○', '11.50 ○'). At 9-10 pt in print, '12 ○' can read as '12°' or '120'. It needs a hairline more space or a smaller, raised ring.

Criterion 12: beer and wine descriptions are category wording, not guest language. 'Dry red wine' / 'Dry white wine' only restate what Malbec and Pinot Grigio are, and 'Crisp pale lager' / 'Hop-forward draft IPA' are close to it. All are verbatim from the manifest, so this is accurate but weak. The cocktail sensory lines are good and consistent.

Criterion 13: the Spanish-first bilingual heads are correct and idiomatic (Cócteles, Destilados, De barril, En lata, Espumosos, Sin alcohol, Por copa). The CERVEZA Y SIDRA / VINO heads are stacked in the label column while wine sits in columns 3-4, so 'Vino · Wine' is detached from its items.

Verified OK against manifest.json: Loess ingredients/garnish/glass (mezcal espadín · Iowa wildflower honey syrup · fresh lemon · ginger; candied ginger · rocks); Carajillo (Licor 43 · fresh espresso; garnish null → 'rocks' only); Spicy Pineapple Margarita (garnish null → 'rocks' only); 'Espolòn Blanco' spelling with grave accent matches the manifest; Olmeca Altos Plata region Los Altos; Ilegal Joven Oaxaca 13; Malbec 12, Pinot Grigio 11, Brut Rosé 13. gates.json also reports a 50/50 DOM diff with 0 differences and a max name-to-price gap of 0.42 em, and every price stays on its name's line via a no-break space.
fixes: Put the proposed ring on the pour line ('1.5 oz pour ○') or remove the pour size until Rob sets it; this clears the content_integrity fail.

Cut the index numerals to about 60% of their size, or hang them in a narrow left gutter, so names, prices and ingredients get about 30 characters of measure. Also bind multi-word ingredients with no-break spaces so 'orange liqueur', 'sweet vermouth' and 'Iowa wildflower honey syrup' never split, and fix the 'snap' widow.
Mark Brut Rosé's serve unit as pending (for example 'glass/bottle ○'), or move it under 'Por copa' only once Rob confirms. Until then, note the missing unit in the proposal.
Replace the bare em-dash regions with an explicit, muted 'region tbc' or omit the line, and add that to the back key.

Move Ilegal Joven's sensory line onto its own card under the class line, and send the designer a note to add a hairline of space before the proposed ring so it cannot be read as a degree sign or zero.

lens: K3 MAPA DE SABOR: how descriptions and prices sit together on the phone PNG (preview-phone.png, 1170x18831). I cropped it with PIL at y 2600-4300, 4300-6000, 6000-7700, 7700-9400, 10000-11700 and 13500-15200, plus the manifest and gates.json.
top_problem: Ingredient lines on the phone break inside ingredients instead of at the middots. Seven lines are affected, and several leave a single orphan word on its own line: 'agave / syrup' (Margarita), 'grapefruit / soda' (Paloma), 'sparkling / mineral water' (Ranch Water), 'fresh / lime' (House Daiquiri), 'fresh / pineapple' (Spicy Pineapple Margarita), 'house roasted-corn / syrup' (Milpa), 'house / demerara syrup' (Brown Butter OF). That splits one ingredient across two lines, which is the one thing this role-ordered stack must not do. Separately, the 2-up spirit cards reserve a two-line name height on every card. Single-line names (Espolon Blanco, Milagro Silver, Patron Silver, Don Julio Blanco, Del Maguey Vida, Ilegal Joven, El Tesoro Anejo) therefore float name+price about 60 css px above their class and oak bar, so the price reads as detached from its data. Name+price pairing is otherwise good (price inline, max gap 0.42 em, proposal ring after the price, matches manifest per the gates.json dom_diff with 0 differences over 50 items). But 'measures correctly' is the price of entry, and the phone rhythm is list-standard. Sources: expanded-v1/manifest.json cocktails rows (e.g. Margarita ingredients ['tequila blanco','orange liqueur','agave syrup','fresh lime'], source 'phg.menu_items + rv f06abb74'), and gates.json dom_diff. No gateway queries were spent, because the panel content source is the manifest.
fixes: Join the words inside each ingredient with no-break spaces (or wrap each ingredient in a nowrap span) so phone lines break only at the ' · ' separators and no single word ('soda', 'lime', 'pineapple', 'syrup') is orphaned.

On the phone, size spirit cards to their content instead of a fixed two-line name slot, or go 1-up below about 430 css px, so class, oak bar and region sit directly under name+price; this also stops Siete Leguas Blanco, Montelobos Espadin and 400 Conejos Espadin from wrapping.

Items with a null garnish print a lone 'rocks' line (Carajillo, Spicy Pineapple Margarita), which reads as an orphan; label it 'served on the rocks' or 'rocks glass' only if the manifest's glass field supports that wording, otherwise merge it onto the ingredient line's tail.

Zero-proof gets only a sensory line and 'Jarritos: Mexican fruit soda; ask for flavors' is server copy, not guest copy; give zero-proof the same stack (ingredients, glass) once the manifest supplies those fields, or flag them as pending rather than shipping an uneven voice.

The '—' region placeholders (Espolon Blanco, Milagro Silver, Casamigos Blanco) print as guest-visible dashes next to a price; resolve them from brands/products before print or drop the region line on those cards so no row looks broken (manifest region_note: 'verify before print').
